ServiceNow jumped 5% and Salesforce gained 4% after Amit Zavery denied any intention to acquire AI customer-service startup Decagon, reaffirming organic growth.

Software ETF IGV rose just 0.9% while QQQ fell 0.7%, revealing selective buying inside enterprise software rather than a broad tech rally.

ServiceNow already fields AI Control Tower, Now Assist, and Build Agent, giving it an internal path into customer-service automation Decagon occupies.

A flat denial of takeover talk is lifting one of the biggest names in enterprise software. ServiceNow (NYSE:NOW) stock is up 5% to $146.93 in midday trading after the company rejected reports that it planned to buy Decagon, a privately held maker of artificial intelligence (AI) customer-service agents.

gorodenkoff / iStock via Getty Images

Meanwhile, Salesforce (NYSE:CRM) stock is up 4% to $245.39, a gain just shy of the advance in ServiceNow stock. Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR) stock is down 0.9% to $199.07, moving opposite both of those software gainers. That split points to selective buying inside the enterprise software group.

Decagon Denial Sparks a Software Rally

ServiceNow moved to shut down the speculation on October 14. Amit Zavery, the company's president, chief product officer and chief operating officer, stated, "We are aware of misinformation in the market today about our acquisition strategy. To be clear, ServiceNow has no interest or intention of purchasing Decagon." Zavery added that the approach to acquisitions is unchanged and that ServiceNow prioritizes organic growth.

Management also sees no major strategic gaps requiring large-scale deals at this time, according to Zavery. Because ServiceNow sells workflow software on recurring subscriptions, the denial of a big acquisition signals where ServiceNow's margins and product roadmap could be heading, and organic growth tends to keep spending tied to products ServiceNow controls end to end.

ServiceNow (NYSE:NOW) and Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR) represent the vanguard of the modern software era. Choosing between these enterprise giants requires a close look at their growth trajectories and current valuations.

ServiceNow focuses on streamlining business operations through its automated workflow platform, connecting departments like HR and IT. Palantir builds data integration systems that help organizations make critical decisions using artificial intelligence. Both companies are essential players in the shift toward data-driven business models as they scale globally.

The case for ServiceNow

ServiceNow provides an AI platform connecting workflows across IT, HR, and customer service for roughly 8,700 enterprise customers. Strategic partners include Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) and Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT), as well as system integrators like Accenture (NYSE:ACN) and Infosys (NYSE:INFY). The company also recently completed the acquisition of Armis to enhance its cyber-asset visibility and AI-powered analytics capabilities.

In FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $13.3 billion, representing a growth of roughly 20.9% compared to the prior year. Net income for the period was close to $1.7 billion, which yields a net margin of approximately 13.2%. This performance reflects a steady expansion from its FY 2024 revenue of approximately $11.0 billion.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was nearly 0.2x. This ratio compares total debt to shareholder equity to measure financial leverage, while the current ratio reached roughly 1.0x. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 35.9% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

The case for Palantir Technologies

Palantir builds software platforms like Foundry and Gotham for AI-driven decision-making in government and tech stocks commercial contexts. The company maintains strategic alliances with partners such as Ondas (NASDAQ:ONDS) through a joint venture called Regna AI. According to its latest annual report, filed for the period ending December 31, 2025, the U.S. Army remains a significant partner for defense intelligence programs.

In FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $4.5 billion, representing a growth of roughly 56.2% compared to the prior year. Net income for the period was close to $1.6 billion, yielding a net margin of approximately 36.3%. This is a notable increase from the net margin of roughly 16.1% reported in FY 2024.

The rise of artificial intelligence has transformed how software companies deliver value and capture market share. Investors choosing between Figma (NYSE:FIG) and Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR) must weigh design collaboration against enterprise-scale data analytics.

Figma offers a cloud-based platform where design teams build digital products together in real time. Palantir provides massive data integration and AI decision-making tools for government and commercial clients. Both companies serve as critical infrastructure in their respective niches within the modern digital economy.

The case for Figma

Figma sells a collaborative design platform used by product teams to prototype and build digital interfaces. It generates revenue from a paid customer base that reached nearly 690,000 in Q1 2026. The company recently adopted an administrator-controlled model for seat upgrades and introduced billing based on AI credits to monetize its new features for enterprise users.

In FY 2025, revenue reached approximately $1.1 billion, representing a growth rate of roughly 41% compared to the prior year. Despite this top-line expansion, the company reported a net loss of close to $1.3 billion during the same period. This resulted in a negative net margin, which measures how much profit a company keeps for every dollar of sales, of about -118.4% among tech stocks in this category.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was approximately 0.1x. This ratio measures total debt against shareholder equity, and a low figure suggests a conservative use of borrowed money. The company generated nearly $246.2 million in free cash flow, which is cash left over after paying for operating costs and capital expenditures. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 544.2% of operating cash flow, meaning reported cash generation is heavily inflated by this non-cash add-back.

The case for Palantir Technologies

Palantir builds software platforms like Foundry and AIP that help organizations integrate vast datasets to make operational decisions. Its strategy focuses on deepening relationships with government agencies and large commercial enterprises through long-term contracts. The company has secured key partnerships, including a joint venture with Ondas (NASDAQ:ONDS) known as Regna AI, focused on specialized defense technology for mission-critical operations.

In FY 2025, revenue reached roughly $4.5 billion, a significant increase of nearly 56.2% over the previous year. The company also reported a net income of approximately $1.6 billion, demonstrating its ability to generate actual profit from its operations. This yielded a net margin of close to 36.3%, showing that it retains more than a third of every dollar it earns as profit after all expenses are paid.

Microsoft has a virtuous cycle of returns. Its dominant market position enables it to generate strong free cash flow, and it reinvests these funds into promising ventures that further strengthen its competitive moat.

title: Palantir (PLTR) Stock Sees Modest Fair Value Lift As Analysts Back AI Execution

Palantir (PLTR) Stock Sees Modest Fair Value Lift As Analysts Back AI Execution
Bailey Pemberton

PLTR
Trade PLTR on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Palantir Technologies is back in focus as fresh valuation work lifts fair value estimates to US$205.27 from US$195.57, signaling a modest reset in where analysts anchor their price targets. Recent research describes strong execution in AI driven software and data platforms, and many firms are tying their higher targets to how Palantir converts AI demand into commercial and sovereign AI contracts. Read on to see how this updated narrative is taking shape and how you can track it as it evolves.

Stay updated as the Fair Value for Palantir Technologies shifts by adding it to your watchlist or portfolio. Alternatively, explore our Community to discover new perspectives on Palantir Technologies.

What Wall Street Has Been Saying
🐂 Bullish Takeaways

Several firms, including Citi, UBS, Baird, Barclays, Mizuho, Northland, Phillip Securities and Deutsche Bank, have lifted Palantir Technologies price targets, with figures across this group ranging from about US$200 to US$265. This reflects growing focus on how its AI platform and data products feed into long term revenue and earnings power.

Goldman Sachs and Deutsche Bank both describe Palantir as ahead of many software peers in turning AI interest into customer value, with Deutsche Bank highlighting what it calls an "exceptional" Q2 report and a strong combination of growth and profitability.

Rosenblatt, DA Davidson and UBS point to commercial traction, including U.S. business momentum, customer pipeline checks and events such as AIPCon 11, as important supports for current valuation frameworks.

Partnerships are another plank of the bullish view. Research from firms covering Zeta Global notes that AthenaOS and joint go to market work with Palantir could help drive larger enterprise contracts and higher spend per customer over time.

🐻 Bearish Takeaways

Jefferies, which raised its target but keeps an Underperform rating, argues the risk reward has become less attractive given tougher growth comparisons into 2027 and moderating international trends, and prefers other AI stocks.

Cantor Fitzgerald maintains a Neutral stance even after what it calls an "exceptional" quarter, signalling that some analysts see Palantir's valuation as already baking in a significant share of the AI opportunity.
